title: ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 Secure Product Development Lifecycle Assessment

display.targetSource: the product's security requirements and customer commitments

targetDimensionLabel: Supplier / product developer (development organisation or product line)
framing: ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 sets out process requirements for the secure development of products used in industrial automation and control systems. The assessment looks at a supplier's product development practices, and the asset owner's environment is outside its scope. The requirements are grouped into eight practices and assessed at maturity levels ML1 to ML4, on the same maturity model as 62443-2-1:2024.
sourceNote: Practice structure and requirement list extracted and verified from the 62443-4-1 document held in the project. Requirement titles are verified; assessor framing is paraphrased; 'verbatimText' and 'otLens' slots are empty for the licence holder to populate. ML anchors are paraphrased. Source: ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 (copyright IEC/ISA).
maturityNote: Reuses the program-maturity-ml scoring family (ML1 Initial / ML2 Managed / ML3 Defined-Practiced / ML4 Improving) defined for 62443-2-1:2024. 4-1 itself uses a maturity model for these practices, so this is the natural fit.

maturityModel.basis: CMMI-SVC; MLs apply independently per requirement; documentation required from ML2 upward

levels.name: Initial
levels.anchor: The process is performed, but ad hoc and often without full documentation, so it is hard to show that it is done consistently over time.
levels.shortAnchor: Performed ad hoc, with little or no documentation.
levels.glossary: The process is ad hoc, if it is performed at all, and depends on the individuals involved.

levels.name: Managed
levels.anchor: Written procedures or training describe how to manage and perform the process. Practice is repeatable and follows documented plans. ML2 is the first level that requires documentation.
levels.shortAnchor: Documented procedures or training, repeatable and managed to plan.
levels.glossary: The process is documented and can be repeated. ML2 is the first level that requires documentation.

levels.name: Defined / Practiced
levels.anchor: The ML2 process is actively practised in product development, and its performance is shown to repeat over time.
levels.shortAnchor: Documented process actively practised, repeatable over time.
levels.glossary: The documented process is used on real product development work and is shown to repeat over time.

levels.name: Improving
levels.anchor: Process metrics show that the process is effective or that its performance is improving. The supplier improves the process through technical, procedural or management changes.
levels.shortAnchor: Measured with metrics and improved over time.
levels.glossary: The process is measured, and the measurements are used to improve it.

maturityModel._display: Show these full definitions ONCE in a help/reference panel, not inline on every requirement. The per-requirement selector uses achievedScale.ordered[].short labels only.

elements.name: Practice 1: Security management
elements.summary: This practice covers how the supplier manages secure product development as a whole, including ownership, scope, expertise, the security of the development environment and continuous improvement.

elements.name: Practice 2: Specification of security requirements
elements.summary: The supplier is expected to capture the product's security context and threat model and turn them into documented, reviewed security requirements.

elements.name: Practice 3: Secure by design
elements.summary: Secure design principles, defence in depth and design review make security part of the product from the start.

elements.name: Practice 4: Secure implementation
elements.summary: Secure coding standards and implementation reviews catch weaknesses as the design is turned into code.

elements.name: Practice 5: Security verification and validation testing
elements.summary: Testing confirms that the security requirements are met and the threats mitigated. It includes vulnerability and penetration testing by suitably independent testers.

elements.name: Practice 6: Management of security-related issues
elements.summary: Security issues found in the product after development have to be received, reviewed, assessed, fixed and disclosed.

elements.name: Practice 7: Security update management
elements.summary: Security updates and patches need to be qualified, documented and delivered reliably and in good time.

elements.name: Practice 8: Security guidelines
elements.summary: Users need documentation that lets them deploy, harden, operate and dispose of the product securely.

requirements.title: Development process
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier follows a defined, documented secure development process that covers the product's lifecycle.
requirements.rationale: A documented process lets secure development be repeated whoever is on the team. Without one, security quality varies from product to product and the supplier cannot give a customer or regulator assurance about it.

requirements.title: Identification of responsibilities
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Responsibilities for security within the development organisation are assigned and written down.
requirements.rationale: Security work with no named owner tends not to get done. Clear responsibilities stop secure development tasks falling between engineering, QA and product management.

requirements.title: Identification of applicability
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier has decided which parts of the process apply to which products and components.
requirements.rationale: Not every product or component needs every part of the process. Deciding where each part applies puts the effort where the product risk calls for it.

requirements.title: Security expertise
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The people doing the work have the security expertise the process needs, through training or recruitment.
requirements.rationale: A secure development process run by people without security skills can look rigorous on paper and still find few real weaknesses.

requirements.title: Process scoping
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The scope of the development process is defined, including which products, versions and components it covers.
requirements.rationale: Where scope is undefined, parts of a product end up treated as someone else's problem.

requirements.title: File integrity
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Files and artefacts in development are protected so that tampering would be detected.
requirements.rationale: If development artefacts can be altered without anyone noticing, an attacker can plant weaknesses before any later control applies, and the tampering is hard to spot afterwards.

requirements.title: Development environment security
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The development environment, including tools, build systems and repositories, is protected against compromise.
requirements.rationale: A compromised build system or repository can poison every product that passes through it, which makes it one of the most damaging forms of supply chain attack.

requirements.title: Controls for private keys
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Private keys used for signing and protection are controlled so they cannot be misused or stolen.
requirements.rationale: Signing keys let users trust that a product or update is genuine. With a stolen key, an attacker can sign malware that passes as legitimate, which undermines trust in every update the supplier issues.

requirements.title: Security requirements for externally provided components
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security requirements apply to externally provided components as well as to code developed in house.
requirements.rationale: Third-party and open source components bring their own vulnerabilities into the product. Unless security requirements also apply to them, weaknesses in code the supplier did not write can undo the supplier's own good practice.

requirements.title: Custom developed components from third-party suppliers
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier manages the security of custom components that third-party suppliers build for it.
requirements.rationale: Outsourced development can bring back the risks the process exists to control. Managing the third party's security holds custom components to the same standard as in-house code.

requirements.title: Assessing and addressing security-related issues
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: There is a defined way to assess and deal with security issues found during development.
requirements.rationale: An issue found during development is cheapest to fix then and does most harm if it ships. A defined route for assessing and fixing these issues stops known problems reaching the customer.

requirements.title: Process verification
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier checks that the development process is followed in practice.
requirements.rationale: A process that is written down and not followed gives false assurance.

requirements.title: Continuous improvement
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The development process is improved over time using lessons learned.
requirements.rationale: Threats and attack techniques change, and a development process that is never improved falls behind the risks the product will face.

requirements.title: Product security context
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product's security context is established, covering how and where the product will be used and the assumptions that follow from that.
requirements.rationale: The same product needs different protection in different settings, so its security requirements depend on how and where it will be used.

requirements.title: Threat model
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier develops and maintains a threat model for the product and uses it to drive the security requirements.
requirements.rationale: A product cannot be required to resist threats nobody has identified. The threat model ties the security requirements to the attack paths the product will face.

requirements.title: Product security requirements
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Documented product security requirements are derived from the security context and the threat model.
requirements.rationale: Security expectations that are not written down cannot be designed or tested against.

requirements.title: Product security requirements content
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The security requirements are detailed enough to be implemented and tested.
requirements.rationale: A requirement too vague to implement or test has little effect, and designers and testers may each read it differently.

requirements.title: Security requirements review
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The security requirements are reviewed to confirm they are complete, correct and consistent.
requirements.rationale: Requirements that are never reviewed carry their gaps and contradictions into the design. A review catches them while they are still cheap to fix.

requirements.title: Secure design principles
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product is designed using established secure design principles.
requirements.rationale: Security built into the design costs far less and works better than security added later, because design is the stage where the product's resilience is easiest to influence.

requirements.title: Defense in depth design
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product's design uses defence in depth, so it does not depend on a single protective measure.
requirements.rationale: A product that relies on one protective measure is fully exposed once that measure is defeated.

requirements.title: Security design review
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The design is reviewed for security before implementation, so flaws are caught early.
requirements.rationale: Design flaws found after implementation are expensive to fix and are often shipped anyway.

requirements.title: Secure design best practices
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier follows secure design practices suited to the product and its technologies.
requirements.rationale: Established design practices capture lessons from other people's failures.

requirements.title: Security implementation review
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The implementation is reviewed for security to check that the code matches the secure design.
requirements.rationale: Insecure implementation can undo a secure design, so the code has to be checked against what the design intended.

requirements.title: Secure coding standards
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Code is written to secure coding standards to avoid known classes of vulnerability.
requirements.rationale: Most code-level vulnerabilities come from a familiar set of mistakes. Secure coding standards steer developers away from those mistakes before the code is written.

requirements.title: Security requirements testing
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product is tested to show that its security requirements are met.
requirements.rationale: A security requirement that is never tested may not be met, and nobody would know until the product is in service.

requirements.title: Threat mitigation testing
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product is tested to show that the threats in the threat model are mitigated.
requirements.rationale: The threat model protects the product only if the finished product mitigates the threats it lists.

requirements.title: Vulnerability testing
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product is tested for vulnerabilities, including with automated tools.
requirements.rationale: Vulnerabilities the supplier misses before release are left for an attacker to find.

requirements.title: Penetration testing
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The product is penetration tested.
requirements.rationale: Penetration testing probes the product as an attacker would and finds problems that testing against each requirement misses.

requirements.title: Independence of testers
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The testers are independent enough from the developers for the results to be credible.
requirements.rationale: Developers who test only their own work tend to miss what they overlooked while building it. Independent testers bring a fresh view and make the results credible.

requirements.title: Receiving notifications of security-related issues
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: There is a defined way to receive reports of security issues from any source.
requirements.rationale: A supplier cannot fix issues it never hears about. A defined reporting channel gets vulnerabilities reported by researchers, customers and others to the people who can act on them.

requirements.title: Reviewing security-related issues
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Reported security issues are reviewed so they are understood.
requirements.rationale: Reports that are received and never reviewed pile up with nothing done. Review turns incoming reports into issues the supplier understands.

requirements.title: Assessing security-related issues
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The severity and impact of each security issue are assessed.
requirements.rationale: Issues differ in seriousness, and treating them all the same either wastes effort or lets a serious one slip. Assessing them sets the order in which they are dealt with.

requirements.title: Addressing security-related issues
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security issues are dealt with through fixes or mitigations.
requirements.rationale: An assessed issue left unfixed is a known vulnerability shipped to every user.

requirements.title: Disclosing security-related issues
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security issues are disclosed responsibly to the people who need to know.
requirements.rationale: The way an issue is disclosed affects whether users can protect themselves before attackers exploit it. Responsible disclosure weighs warning users against giving attackers a head start.

requirements.title: Periodic review of security defect management practices
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The defect management practice is reviewed periodically to keep it effective.
requirements.rationale: A defect management practice that is never reviewed drifts over time like any other process.

requirements.title: Security update qualification
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security updates are qualified so they are known to work and do not introduce new problems.
requirements.rationale: An update that breaks the product or brings in new flaws can do more harm than the vulnerability it fixes. Qualification shows the fix is safe to apply, which matters especially in OT, where stability comes first.

requirements.title: Security update documentation
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security updates are documented so users understand what they fix and how to apply them.
requirements.rationale: Users cannot apply an update sensibly without knowing what it changes. Good documentation lets an operator assess a patch and schedule it with confidence.

requirements.title: Dependent component or operating system security update
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Updates to dependent components and operating systems are handled as well as updates to the product's own code.
requirements.rationale: A product inherits the vulnerabilities of its dependencies and operating system, so their updates have to be handled as well.

requirements.title: Security update delivery
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security updates reach users through a dependable delivery mechanism.
requirements.rationale: A fix protects users only once it reaches the installed product, so the supplier needs a dependable way to deliver it.

requirements.title: Timely delivery of security patches
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: Security patches are delivered in a time that reflects the risk they address.
requirements.rationale: A patch that arrives long after a risk becomes known leaves attackers a window to exploit it. Timing delivery to the severity of the issue narrows that window, although OT users still need time to test a patch before they apply it.

requirements.title: Product defense in depth
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier provides guidance on the product's own defence in depth features.
requirements.rationale: Users cannot use protective features they do not know about.

requirements.title: Defense in depth measures expected in the environment
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier documents the defence in depth measures the product expects its operating environment to provide.
requirements.rationale: Every product assumes the surrounding environment will provide some protection. If users are not told what those assumptions are, the protection may be missing. Stating the expected measures lets the operator check its environment against them.

requirements.title: Security hardening guidelines
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier provides hardening guidelines so users can configure the product securely.
requirements.rationale: A product in its default configuration is rarely as secure as it can be. Hardening guidelines let an operator close that gap, and in OT this is often the most practical security improvement available.

requirements.title: Secure disposal guidelines
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier provides guidance on disposing of the product securely, so that retiring it does not leak sensitive data.
requirements.rationale: Equipment retired without proper disposal still holds configuration, credentials and data useful to an attacker.

requirements.title: Secure operation guidelines
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier provides guidance on operating the product securely once it is in service.
requirements.rationale: A securely built product can still be operated insecurely. Operating guidance helps the operator keep the product secure in day-to-day service as well as at installation.

requirements.title: Account management guidelines
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The supplier provides guidance on managing the product's user accounts and roles.
requirements.rationale: Default and unmanaged accounts are a common way into otherwise sound products. Account management guidance helps operators avoid the shared and standing credentials that are common in OT.

requirements.title: Documentation review
requirements.evidencePrompt: Record the documented process, the evidence that it is followed, and why you chose this maturity level.
requirements.hint: The user documentation is reviewed to confirm that its security guidance is accurate and complete.
requirements.rationale: Wrong or incomplete security guidance misleads the users who are trying to follow it.

achievedScale._note: ONE control per requirement. Consultant picks one value. 'not-met' is the bottom of the scale; ML1-4 are increasing maturity; 'unknown' and 'na' are non-scoring states shown alongside.

targetOverlay._note: Optional. Off by default. When enabled, each requirement gains an optional target ML. When off, the report shows the achieved-ML profile only.

_contentNote: 47 requirements across 8 practices, verified from the standard. Paraphrased hint (what it is) and rationale (why it matters) on each; verbatimText and otLens empty for population from the licensed standard. Supplier-side instrument; pairs with the supplier-advisory references.
_relatedWork: Designed to sit alongside the supplier discovery references and question banks as the scored core of the supplier-evaluation toolkit. Also the authoritative target for 'secure development' cross-references currently pointing loosely at 2-1 ORG 2.3 (CAF A4.b, NIS2 measure (e)).
seriesContext: ISA/IEC 62443 is a series of standards divided according to who is responsible for what. This part, 62443-4-1, covers the product supplier and the development process behind a product. Its companion 62443-4-2 covers the security capabilities of the product itself, and the 3-x parts cover the system built from those products.
